page.title: Webinar Production Checklist Guide
page.description: A practical checklist covering format decisions, run‑of‑show ownership, rehearsal timing, backup streams and delivery steps for webinars.
page.h1: What belongs on a webinar production checklist?
page.definition: A webinar production checklist is a structured list of tasks, owners and deadlines that ensures the format, run of show, speaker preparation, technical rehearsal, backup stream and post‑event delivery are all assigned and completed before going live and recorded for replay distribution.
page.quick_answer: Assign a single producer to own the run of show, schedule a full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before, and prepare a backup stream and replay delivery within 24 to 48 hours.

sections.h2: Which format and audience outcome should I lock first?

blocks.p: Lock the format and the desired audience outcome before any other decision. Choose between a single‑speaker presentation, a panel discussion, a fireside chat or a demo‑driven session and match it to a clear outcome such as lead generation, product education or community building.

sections.h2: Who owns the run of show and each production workstream?

blocks.p: Assign a single producer to own the run of show and map eight workstreams each with one owner.

sections.h2: What rehearsal and technical checks are required before going live?

blocks.p: Run a full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before and a technical check 60 minutes before going live.

sections.h2: Which tools handle planning, registration and follow‑up?

blocks.p: Use a project board for the plan, a registration platform for sign‑ups and a CRM for follow‑up.

ul: Asana or Monday.com for the plan

sections.h2: What deliverables and timelines should I expect from a production partner?

blocks.p: A production partner delivers a run of show, speaker brief, branded assets, live producer, Q&A moderation, backup stream, edited recording and clips within three to four weeks for a webinar.

ul: Branded slide template and lower thirds

faq.q: How far in advance should I start planning a webinar?
faq.a: Start planning a webinar three to four weeks before the live date; for a summit or conference allow six to eight weeks. This lead time covers briefing, speaker coordination, platform setup, rehearsal and backup‑stream testing and ensures all deliverables are approved before go‑live.

faq.q: What is the typical cost range for a moderated webinar production?
faq.a: Moderated webinars typically cost $2,500 to $7,500 per production, depending on speaker count, branding complexity and whether a backup stream is included. The price also reflects rehearsal time, live moderation and post‑event editing. Agencies may quote higher for custom graphics or multi‑camera setups.

faq.q: Do I need a backup stream for every webinar?
faq.a: A backup stream is recommended for any live event because a single point of failure can drop the audience; the extra encoder adds minimal cost and protects the recording. It also satisfies compliance requirements for regulated industries. Plan the backup during the technical check 60 minutes before go‑live.

faq.q: When should the replay be sent to attendees?
faq.a: Send the replay within 24 to 48 hours after the session ends while the content is still fresh; this window maximises engagement and supports lead‑nurture workflows. Include a short highlight clip and a call‑to‑action for the next event. Automate delivery through your CRM to avoid manual effort.
